headline: Delayed action on approximately $3.45 million staff device technology lease to check its interest rate.
summary: Members discussed replacing staff devices under a proposed multi-year technology lease of approximately $3.45 million over five years. The proposed teacher devices are MacBook Neos at approximately $800 each, and the lease would replace all devices at once. Members delayed action until more information is obtained on whether the lease interest rate can be reduced.

## Joint Finance & Curriculum Subcommittee Meeting

Wednesday, October 7, 2026

City Hall, Council Chamber

5:30 p.m.

- **Finance Subcommittee Members Present:** Chairperson Bahou and Mr. Conway. Ms. Martin was absent.
- **Curriculum Subcommittee Members Present:** Mr. Bahou and Ms. Delrossi. Chairperson Martin was absent.
- **School Department Personnel Present:** Dr. Pinto, Assistant Superintendent; Mr. Limperis, MIS Director

---

Chairperson Bahou called the meeting to order at 5:39 p.m. The following agenda items were discussed:

- Staff Device Refresh Strategy & Evaluation Report

Chairperson Bahou opened the meeting by stating that the evening's discussion would focus on the proposed multi-year technology lease agreement, which would cost Lowell Public Schools approximately $3.45 million over five years.

Mr. Limperis stated that current staff devices are reaching the end of their recommended operational lifespan, resulting in security vulnerabilities, software and operating system incompatibility, and decreased device performance. He noted that current curricula are largely digital and rely on web-based multimedia tools. He emphasized the need to ensure that staff have continuous access to reliable devices to support the delivery of high-quality instruction to students. Implementing a rolling refresh cycle, he explained, would shift expenses from irregular and costly capital expenditures to more predictable long-term operating costs.

Mr. Limperis stated that the proposed teacher devices would be MacBook Neos, costing approximately $800 each. He also discussed AppleCare+, which provides two repairs per year at no additional cost. He noted that teachers have been using their current district-issued devices for nearly seven years and that Apple stops providing software updates after seven years, making the devices more vulnerable to security issues. He stated that delaying replacement could ultimately cost the district an additional $20 to $30 per device, as costs have increased significantly.

Mr. Limperis also discussed Chromebooks. He stated that the MacBook Neo was selected based on cost and financial predictability and that it has the lowest upfront cost among the qualified platforms.

Chairperson Bahou asked what percentage of the current Macs would need to be replaced.

Mr. Limperis stated that it was difficult to determine an exact percentage but noted that all of the current devices were purchased in 2020 and are no longer receiving updates.

Chairperson Conway asked whether the expected lifespan of a Chromebook is approximately six years.

Mr. Limperis stated that it is difficult to determine an exact lifespan but estimated that Chromebooks typically last approximately five to six years.

Ms. Delrossi asked whether the cloud could can be accessed on an Apple and Google devices.

Mr. Limperis stated it can be accessed from both.

Chairperson Bahou asked the Apple representative how long the MacBook Neo could realistically be expected to last.

Ms. McLaughlin, an Apple representative, stated that there is not yet sufficient data available because the MacBook Neo was only released in March. She noted that Apple products typically have a long life and retain their residual value.

Mr. Limperis added that the district could turn in the older Mac devices to a third-party vendor and receive approximately $210 per device.

Chairperson Bahou asked whether the district could implement the replacement on a staggered basis by refreshing devices each year.

Mr. Limperis stated that the proposed lease would allow all of the devices to be replaced at once.

Mr. Conway stated that if the district has the funds available this year, the replacement should be completed now because funding may not be available in subsequent years.

Chairperson Bahou asked whether the interest rate on the lease could be removed or lowered.

Ms. McLauglin, an Apple representative, stated that Apple does not offer zero-percent financing but said she could follow up to determine whether any other options were available.

**Ms. Delrossi moved to delay action until additional information could be obtained regarding whether the interest rate on the lease could be reduced and to accept the report as a report of progress. The motion was seconded by Mr. Conway. The motion passed with 3 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Martin).**

**Mr. Conway moved to adjourn at 6:22 p.m.; the motion was seconded by Ms. Delrossi. The motion passed with 3 yeas, 1 absent (Martin).**

Respectfully submitted,

Dr. Pinto, Assistant Superintendent of Finance for Liam Skinner, Superintendent
